full_judgment:
3. Defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material averments made in the plaint. He contended, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable in its present form and the same was barred by limitation. The registered "Nirupan Patra" dated 25-3-1981 is a genuine document by which Obaidur Rahman alias Abidur Rahman expressed his desire to dispose of his properties in the manner as contained therein. The plaintiffs-appellants knew everything about the "Nirupan Patra". The "Nirupan Patra" has already been acted upon and the plaintiffs-appellants and the defendants are in possession of the properties as per the terms of the "Nirupan Patra". The deed in question is a "Nirupan Patra" but not "Osiatnama". The plaintiffs have no right, title and interest in the suit land and, as such, the plaintiffs' suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 II. For that the High Court Division committed serious, illegality in setting aside the judgment of the appellate Court without considering whether exhibit-2 (Nirupan Patra) is capable of creating entitlement in immovable property in favour of the defendant respondents in question. It has been found from the exhibit-2 and it can be gathered from the recital therein that it is an arrangement which as per recital is in consonance with wasiat of the testator in question about the nature of this exhibit-2 and to what extent it can become effective under section 5 of the Transfer of Property Act. A Will is not a transfer of property under section 89 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. There can be transfer by registered instruments. Under section 89(6)(b) transfer does not include partition. The other kind of transfer can be by way of bequest. Such bequest must be construed in the light of the personal law of the party. But this vital fact of this case has not been considered by the High Court Division and, as such, interference is called for by this Division. 

 III. For that under Islamic law a testator cannot deprive his lawful heirs of more than 1/3 of his estate. A bequest to an heir is under no circumstances valid and under such circumstances the instant bequest being made to the heirs in the guise of a Nirupan Patra or "Deed of (future) determination and arrangement" is abinitio void. Exhibit-2 has in fact deprived the plaintiffs of their inalienable right of inheritance under the personal law to which they are subject and the impugned Nirupan Patra is a device to deprive the plaintiffs and considering all the facts and circumstances it cannot be treated as an ideal instrument of testament and, as such, the High Court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute and in dismissing the suit attaching importance to the disputed deed in question which is not based on proper law and evidence and interference is called for by this Division." 

 8. Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of respondents made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He also submitted that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division considering the evidence and materials on record came to the decision that the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate Court reversing the judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court is not a proper judgment of reversal inasmuch as the appellate Court has not adverted to all the findings arrived at by the trial Court as such the High Court Division rightly set aside the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate Court and the judgment and decree dated 31-10-1992 passed by the Assistant Judge, Boalkhali, Chittagong in Other Class Suit No. 59 of 1990 have been restored rightly. He further submitted that the High Court Division after hearing the parties and considering the judgments and order of the courts below and also considering the evidence and materials on record came to the conclusion that the plaintiff did not claim any relief against the deed in question, she simply stated in her examination-in-chief that she has suffered loss by the deed in question. She did not adduce any evidence claiming the deed in question to be created by false personification and also held that the deed was executed and registered on commission and the deed having been executed and registered on commission there is no scope to say that the said deed was forged unless any positive evidence is adduced; that there was no evidence available on record to declare the deed to be a forged or void one, the learned Single Judge has held that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge now Joint District Judge being the last Court of fact committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in declaring the deed in question to be void as such the learned Single Judge rightly set aside the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate Court which need not be interfered by this Court. He also submitted that the parties to the deed in question are the heirs and legal representatives of late Obaidur Rahman, so the deed has been in favour of the co-sharers of Obaidur Rahman by Obaidur Rahman himself, as such the High Court Division held that the plaintiffs may seek remedy in a properly instituted partition suit and made the Rule absolute in Civil Revision No. 2381 of 1996 which should not be interfered by this Division in this appeal. He lastly submitted that the High Court Division considering evidence of the plaintiffs witnesses and defendants witnesses and facts and circumstances of the case came to the finding that there is merit in the Rule, and accordingly made the Rule absolute, thus restoring the judgment and order of the trial Court dated 29th March, 2007, which should not be reversed in this appeal for ends of justice. 

 10. A Will is a document in which a person specifies the method to be applied in the management and distribution of his estate after his death. The 'Nirupon Patra' also referred to as the 'Arpan Nama' by the appellate Court, is precisely a registered deed dated 25-3-1981 in which the executant, Obaidur Rahman-predecessor of both the, plaintiffs and defendants detailed how his land measuring 868½ decimals was to be distributed after his death. The deed was exhibited at the time of the trial. The plaintiffs claimed that the deed was fraudulently created by forcibly taking the executant's signatures on blank stamp papers. The defendants claimed that the deed was duly executed arid, registered on commission. 

 13. It appears, from the records that the suit was filed by Noorjahan Begum on behalf of herself and her 4 minor children seeking a declaration that the registered deed No. 1608 dated 25-3-1981 "Nirupan patra" (said deed) is illegal, forged, void and inoperative. The deed in question was executed by Abdur Rahman @ Obaidur Rahman, the husband of plaintiff No. 1 and father of plaintiff Nos. 2-5. By this deed the executant sought to transfer 868½ decimals of land in favour of plaintiff Nos. 1 to 5 and his 4 children from his first wife-3 sons(defendant No. 1-3) and 1 daughter (defendant No. 4). In the said deed the executant stated, inter alia, that he was executing the deed in order that his children shall live happily and peacefully and amicably divide his property accordingly to his will (অছিয়ত). He also stated that as long as he is alive the title and possession of the property Will remain with him. Then he went on to describe in detail how the property would be divided amongst his second wife and 8 children from his 2 wives. Thus there can be no doubt that deed in question is a Will. 

 15. So far as Mahomedan Law is concerned, a testator may lawfully transfer 1/1 of his property to any person (third party), other than his heirs. Any transfer in excess of 1/3 would not be valid unless the heirs consented after the death of the testator. In this regard we may refer to Institutes of Mussalman Law by Nawab AFM Abdur Rahman (1977). In paragraph 471, at page 259 it is stated as follows: 

 Where some of the heirs, who are not legatees, assent, such assent Will take effect with regard to them only and proportionately to their shares in the estate. 

 "A bequest, to a stranger (or non-heir) is valid to the extent of one-third of the testator's estate, but it may be validated respecting a larger proportion with the assent of the heirs after the death of the testator."
